title: The flip
rule: Start from the yo-form, drop the -o, swap the vowel: -ar verbs take e, -er and -ir verbs take a. That stem is the subjunctive, and it is also every ustedes command, every usted command, and every negative command.
exception: Tú positive commands do not flip. They are the él present form: levanta, cree, ven, di, ten, haz, pon, sal, sé, ve.

your_misses.correct: no tengan miedo / no tengas miedo

your_misses.rule: tú positive = él form of arrepentirse

trigger_reminder: You already place 'que' correctly after querer, pedir, esperar, no creer, para. The trigger layer is not the gap. Only the verb after 'que' changes.

title: Sound and stress
rule: Every word has exactly one stressed syllable, and the language has one default: ends in a vowel, n, or s → stress the second-to-last syllable; ends in any other consonant → stress the last. The tilde is not decoration — it is a flag that says THIS WORD BREAKS THE DEFAULT. Say the word out loud, find the stress, check it against the default: match → no tilde; break → tilde on the stressed vowel.

mechanism.op: pair: tilde marks the stressed word
mechanism.output: él / tú / sé / más / sí / qué

exception: The pairs (él/el, tú/tu, sé/se, más/mas, sí/si, qué/que) ignore the sound rules: both words sound the same. The tilde marks the one that carries stress in the sentence — the pronoun, the verb, the question word.

your_misses.said: mi mama me pregunto si tu vas
your_misses.rule: mamá breaks the default; preguntó past; tú pronoun
your_misses.correct: mi mamá me preguntó si tú vas

your_misses.said: yo se que el no puede, ojala que si
your_misses.rule: sé/él/sí are the stressed pair-words; ojalá breaks
your_misses.correct: yo sé que él no puede, ojalá que sí

your_misses.rule: a ver = look and see; jóvenes esdrújula
your_misses.correct: a ver si vienen los jóvenes

your_misses.rule: iba has no h — haber does

your_misses.said: yo conosco, ay muchos como el
your_misses.rule: zc before o; hay = there is; él pronoun
your_misses.correct: yo conozco, hay muchos como él

trigger_reminder: Your ear already knows where the stress falls — you say these words right every Sunday. The gap is only the flag on paper.

title: Gender exceptions
rule: Your agreement engine already works — once you know the gender, every adjective lands right. The gap is the lookup table, and it has exactly three corrupted zones: Greek -ma nouns are masculine (el problema); a handful of shortened -o nouns are feminine (la mano, la foto); and feminine nouns that START with a stressed a- take EL in the singular only, while staying feminine everywhere else (el agua fría, las aguas).

mechanism.output: el problema grande, el drama es
la mano derecha, la foto vieja

mechanism.op: stressed a- → EL singular, feminine agreement
mechanism.output: el agua fría → las aguas frías
la cura para el drama (never el cura = priest)

mechanism.input: el/la líder, el/la joven, el/la testigo
mechanism.op: common gender: article does the work
mechanism.output: la líder del grupo de mujeres

exception: EL agua is not masculine — it is feminine wearing el to avoid the a-a collision. The adjective tells the truth: el agua fría, el alma perdida, mucha hambre.

your_misses.rule: stressed a-: el singular, feminine agreement

trigger_reminder: You scored the agreement engine solid. This unit is a 50-word lookup table, not a new rule.

title: Se lo
rule: Two pronouns travel as one unit, in one fixed order: person before thing (me/te/se/nos before lo/la/los/las). When le or les would land in front of lo/la, it becomes SE — the language refuses le lo. The unit never splits: in front of a conjugated verb, glued to the end of an affirmative command or infinitive.

mechanism.op: negative command: unit moves in front

mechanism.input: Voy a decir la verdad (a ustedes)
mechanism.op: infinitive: glue or front — both correct
mechanism.output: Voy a decírselo / Se lo voy a decir

mechanism.op: pon + se + lo, tilde keeps the stress

exception: The glued forms grow a tilde because the stress must not move: di → díselo, pon → pónselo, deja → déjaselo. That is Unit 2 working inside Unit 4.

your_misses.rule: le + la → se la; the thing must appear
the direct object never drops: it becomes lo

trigger_reminder: You avoid se lo by rebuilding the sentence without pronouns. The congregation hears the difference — this unit makes the short form automatic.

title: Border to pulpit
rule: You already hear the anglicism — detection scored 5 of 6. The gap is the replacement reflex: every border loanword has a standard Mexican counterpart, and the swap is one word for one word — the sentence stays yours. Border Spanish is not wrong; it is a register. The pulpit register swaps the word.

mechanism.input: parquear la troca en la yarda
mechanism.output: estacionar la camioneta en el patio

exception: Some words stay: nomás, ratito, platicar are Northern Mexican, not anglicisms — they belong in your pulpit. The false friends are the trap: realizar, atender, soportar, aplicar all exist in Spanish with DIFFERENT meanings.

your_misses.rule: solicitar is the verb for applications

trigger_reminder: Detection is solid — trust your ear. When it pings, the standard word is one swap away, and the Swap drill is building that reflex.

title: Formulas
rule: Free production does not start from a blank page — it starts from frames you already own in English and now own in Spanish. A prayer is assembled, not improvised: address God (tú) → invite or thank → petition with pedir/querer que + the flip → seal it (en el nombre de Jesús, amén). Fourteen formula families cover everything you do in a service; master the frames and the free part is just the middle.

mechanism.op: tú to God, ustedes to the church
mechanism.output: Señor, Tú estás invitado a este lugar
te pedimos que selles y asegures
Que el Señor los bendiga y los guarde
Confieso que he hablado cuando debí escuchar
En el nombre de Jesús, amén

memorize: En el nombre de Jesús, amén.
exception: The idioms flagged [FLAG] do not translate — they get replaced: 'my heart for this message' → mi anhelo con este mensaje; 'get over ourselves' → dejar el ego a un lado. Drop the image, keep the meaning.

your_misses.correct: Señor, bendice este tiempo en Tu Palabra… te pedimos que… en el nombre de Jesús, amén.

trigger_reminder: The cloze drill blanks the load-bearing verb in each formula — almost always a flip you learned in Unit 1.

title: The manuscript
rule: The sermon is written in frames you own and corrected by native ears, one paragraph a day. Draft with the systems running: after every trigger, flip the verb; say each word aloud and flag the default-breakers with a tilde; keep se-lo pairs glued; swap the border words. Then read the paragraph to a real person and bring every correction back to Debrief — the manuscript is finished when the corrections stop.

mechanism.op: triggers → flip; stress → tilde; loanwords → swap

mechanism.input: read it to a native speaker

memorize: Aquí está mi reto para esta semana.
Vayan en paz, vayan en amor, vayan en victoria.
exception: Scripture is never drafted — NBLA strings go in verbatim, from the verified list under Track.
trigger_reminder: Week 12 you preach it. Every system in this app exists so that this paragraph-a-day loop works.
